title: Moringa Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Moringa Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Moringa nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in malunggay, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Moringa nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your malunggay (moringa) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, boron and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Nitrogen deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for moringa
heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which moringa nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a moringa nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest moringa nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in moringa

In a seedling study from Yunnan, nitrogen shortage gave the earliest and clearest signs of all nutrients: the whole plant turned light yellow and stayed small and weak. The older leaflets pale first, as in other plants. New shoots are short and few, so leaf harvests are light. You see it most at this stage: any stage, but worst in plants cut often for leaves, since every harvest takes nitrogen away.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in malunggay
Frequent leaf harvests without feeding, sandy soils low in organic matter, and heavy rain. A Brazilian study found nitrogen and potassium were the nutrients moringa seedlings took up most.
How to tell it apart

Red mites, the worst pest in a Tarlac malunggay trial, speckle leaves pale and yellow. Look for tiny mites and webbing under the leaflets. To be sure, A soil test before planting. Plants that green up and push new shoots within two weeks after urea or manure confirm it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

TNAU gives 15 kg of compost per pit at planting, then 45 grams of nitrogen per pit 3 months after sowing (as part of 45:15:30 grams of NPK) and another 45 grams of nitrogen at 6 months. 45 grams of nitrogen is about 100 grams of Urea 46 0 0. After cutting back, TNAU gives 45:15:30 grams of NPK per plant with 25 kg of manure. Water after feeding.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add compost or manure after every few leaf harvests and feed in small, regular doses.
Potassium deficiency in moringa

No clear malunggay description was found: in the Yunnan seedling study, plants short of potassium showed no obvious signs, only slower growth. So this follows general plant signs. Older leaflets yellow at the tips and edges, then the edges dry brown. In pod crops, pods stay short and fill poorly. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees and plants cut often for leaves.
Why potassium deficiency happens in malunggay
Sandy, leached soils and heavy harvests. The Brazilian study found potassium was the second most taken up nutrient after nitrogen.
How to tell it apart
Red mites, the worst pest in a Tarlac malunggay trial, speckle leaves pale and yellow. Look for tiny mites and webbing under the leaflets. To be sure, A soil test for potash. A leaf test helps.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

TNAU gives 30 grams of potash per pit at 3 months as part of 45:15:30 grams of NPK, and again after cutting back. 30 grams of potash is about 50 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60. For drip, TNAU applies nitrogen and potash as urea and muriate of potash.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a complete fertilizer such as 14 14 14 or add potash with every feeding.
Phosphorus deficiency in moringa

No clear malunggay description was found: the Yunnan seedling study saw no obvious signs, only slower growth. So this follows general plant signs. Young plants grow slowly and root poorly. Leaves stay dull dark green and older ones may turn purplish. Branching and flowering are poor. You see it most at this stage: seedlings and young plants after planting.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in malunggay
Acid soils that hold phosphorus and planting without manure or phosphate. TNAU notes moringa does best on deep sandy loam soil at pH 6.5 to 8.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage also slows growth, but leaves turn pale instead of dark. Cold and waterlogged soil also slow young plants and can purple the leaves. To be sure, A soil test for phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Mix phosphate into the pit at planting. TNAU gives 15 grams of phosphate per pit at 3 months as part of 45:15:30 grams of NPK. Applies phosphorus to the soil at planting. 15 grams of phosphate is about 75 grams of Superphosphate 0 20 0 or 33 grams of Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0. Lime very acid soils.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add compost and a phosphate fertilizer to every planting pit.
Boron deficiency in moringa

No malunggay particular description was found, so this follows general plant signs. New leaves and shoot tips grow twisted or stunted and the tip can die. Flowers drop and few pods set. A TNAU trial at Periyakulam found that a 0.2 percent boric acid spray gave the most panicles, flowers per panicle and pods per panicle, which suggests boron limits pod set. You see it most at this stage: flowering and pod setting in trees grown for pods.
Why boron deficiency happens in malunggay
Sandy, leached soils, soils of high pH, and dry spells. In general, boron is less available at high pH, as the University of Delaware guide notes.
How to tell it apart

Pod fly and bud worms also cause flower and pod drop. Look for maggots in pods and caterpillars in buds, as TNAU lists these as main moringa pests. To be sure, A soil test with pH and boron. Spray a few trees and compare pod set.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Spray boric acid at 0.2 percent (2 grams per liter) at the vegetative, flowering and pod setting stages, as in the TNAU Periyakulam trial. Borax or Solubor can also be used. Follow the label. Boron is toxic in excess, so do not raise the rate.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add compost every season, and give a boron spray before flowering where pod set is poor.
Zinc deficiency in moringa

No malunggay particular description was found, so this follows general plant signs. New leaflets come out small and yellow between the veins while the veins stay green, and the shoots stay short and bunched. In the TNAU Periyakulam trial, a mixed micronutrient spray did best and a ferrous sulfate plus zinc sulfate spray came second for plant growth and pods. You see it most at this stage: new flushes after cutting back, and young plants.
Why zinc deficiency happens in malunggay
High pH soils, which hold zinc, as the University of Delaware guide notes, and heavy phosphate use. TNAU notes moringa is often grown on soils up to pH 8, where zinc is less available.
How to tell it apart

Iron shortage also yellows new leaves between the veins, often on the same high pH soils. The two are often sprayed together. To be sure, A soil test with pH and a leaf test. Spray a few plants and compare the next flush.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray Zinc sulfate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter) at the vegetative, flowering and pod setting stages, as in the TNAU Periyakulam trial. It was used together with Ferrous sulfate at 1 percent plus 0.1 percent citric acid. Do not mix zinc with phosphate fertilizer in one dose.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add compost and avoid overusing phosphate fertilizer.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any moringa nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your malunggay needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Moringa nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my malunggay leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: the whole plant turns light yellow, new leaves come small, and plants stay thin and weak. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in moringa?
items.a: TNAU gives 15 kg of compost per pit at planting, then 45 grams of nitrogen per pit 3 months after sowing (as part of 45:15:30 grams of NPK) and another 45 grams of nitrogen at 6 months. 45 grams of nitrogen is about 100 grams of Urea 46 0 0.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in moringa?
items.a: TNAU gives 30 grams of potash per pit at 3 months as part of 45:15:30 grams of NPK, and again after cutting back. 30 grams of potash is about 50 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in moringa?
items.a: Mix phosphate into the pit at planting. TNAU gives 15 grams of phosphate per pit at 3 months as part of 45:15:30 grams of NPK.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my malunggay lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the moringa nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
